messages.text: Will a power spike fry the whole miner?

Great question — this is actually one of the Rev 6.1's real differentiators.

**The onboard F1 fuse has your back.**

There's a small automotive-style blade fuse — the **F1 fuse** — sitting right on the board, next to the yellow XT30 power input. It's the first thing a spike hits.

- A power spike → **F1 blows**, absorbing the hit
- The B.1370 chips, ESP32-S3, and LCD behind it? **Protected**
- Fix: swap a $0.50 fuse, not a $249 miner

Cheaper boards skip this entirely — a spike goes straight through and cooks the electronics. Here it costs you a fuse.

The **MEANWELL LRS-350-12 PSU** (included) also helps — it's a clean industrial supply, not a cheap switching brick prone to voltage irregularities.
Is the included power supply actually reliable?

Short answer: **yes, and it's genuinely overbuilt for this job.**

The **MEANWELL LRS-350-12** is a 350 W / 29 A industrial-grade supply (UL/CE/UKCA certified) feeding a miner that draws **~100 W at full tilt** — so it's loafing at roughly **30% of its rated cap····.**

Why that matters:
- Supplies run coolest, quietest, and longest well below their ceiling
- Cheap competitors bundle ~99–124 W bricks that are already maxed out just running the miner at stock — no margin at all
- A maxed brick running 24/7 is, as JD puts it, *"very likely to fail"* — and can take the miner with it when it does

**The M. ships in the box** — no separate purchase, no hunting for a compatible supply. Unbox, plug in, run.

It also leaves serious headroom if you ever want to overclock via the open firmware. You won't need a new PSU for that.
